ev.q: During 2018, rural Black persons received a higher percentage of late-stage HIV diagnosis (25.2%)
viral suppression within 6 months of diagnosis was highest in metropolitan areas (63.8%)
linked to care within 1 month of diagnosis was 76.7% in rural areas
During 2018, rural Black persons received a higher percentage of late-stage HIV diagnosis (25.2%)
Males were less likely than were females to be linked to care, regardless of area
CDC analyzed data reported to NHSS for Black persons aged ≥13 years who received a diagnosis of HIV during 2018

methods_quotes.q: Data were statistically adjusted by using multiple imputation techniques to account for missing HIV transmission categories
Linkage to care within 1 month of diagnosis was measured by documentation of one or more CD4 counts
Viral suppression within 6 months of HIV diagnosis was defined as a viral load of <200 HIV RNA copies/mL
Analyses were conducted using SAS (version 9.4; SAS Institute).
Data not displayed because the numbers were too small to be meaningful.
